judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard identification of parties; the only soft edge is 'shall be effective as hereinafter provided', which defers effectiveness to an unspecified later term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17 says the Agreement 'shall be effective as of the date first above written', so the deferral in the preamble is answered rather than contradicted, though the two sit awkwardly together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite payment obligation of $2,000 tied to execution; nothing in the wording is open to two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is cast as a recital yet imposes an operative payment duty, and it must be read alongside the separate per-well location fee in Section 3(B)(2) — a classic recital/operative-text seam, though the two amounts are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '2000' radius circle surrounding Well KF-1053' and the garbled tract numbers leave the excepted area defined only by reference to a plat, but the exception itself is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2(D) repeats the exclusion using 'centered around' rather than 'surrounding' and Exhibit A's footnote uses 'sorrounding'; a recital reserving rights against an operative earning clause is the kind of seam courts probe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain incorporation list; the only wrinkle is calling Exhibit C a 'Geological Requirement Letter' when the attached document is headed 'Geological Requirements'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibits C and D are undated forms with blanks, so incorporating them 'as part of this Farmout Agreement' creates minor friction with Sections 3(D) and 4.A which assume completed terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining a 'completed well' to include a well 'plugged and abandoned, if a dry hole' is counter-intuitive and could be argued either way about what 'completes' means.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term never reappears verbatim; the operative text uses 'completed as a well capable of production in paying quantities' (3(D)) and 'drills and completes the test well' (Section 16), so the definition could make a dry hole satisfy Section 16.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional regulatory definition; the 'e.g.' list is illustrative and does not narrow the general term in any contested way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used consistently in 3(A)(1) and 3(B)(1) for well location, with no competing acreage concept other than the 80/40-acre circles of 2(D), which serve a different function.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is circular — an earning well is one by which Farmee is 'entitled to receive' an assignment — but it is short and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The phrase 'earning well' is never used anywhere else in the instrument, leaving a defined term with no operative work; the earning mechanics live instead in 3(D) and 2(D).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Capable of producing in paying quantities' and the 80/40-acre 'circle centered around' each well are the classic contested measures of what acreage is earned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 3(E) (depths earned), 3(D)(1) (which points back to 2(D)) and Exhibit D's blank 'acre circle', and with the drilling-unit concept in 2(B) which measures acreage differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'and other similar burdens on production' is a catch-all after an enumeration, the standard ejusdem generis problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Lease burdens' appears nowhere else in the Agreement, so the catch-all has no operative consequence; Section 4.A handles the overriding royalty independently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise numeric definition from surface to 4,000 feet with nothing vague in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(E) caps earned depths at '100' below the total depth drilled, not to exceed 4,000'', and 3(C) speaks of wells lost 'prior to being drilled to Contract Depth' although no clause actually obliges Farmee to reach Contract Depth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition tied to the first well drilled; no term in it carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches 3(A) and Section 16's reference to 'the test well', with no competing usage elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Capable of producing in commercial quantities' uses a standard found nowhere else and undefined, differing from the 'paying quantities' test used throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7(A) imposes shut-in royalties on wells capable of production 'whether or not such well has already produced', directly contradicting this definition's requirement that a shut-in well 'has previously produced'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward temporal definition; the OCR misspelling 'subseauent' is scanning noise rather than a drafting error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 3(B), though 3(B) conditions Subsequent Wells on the test well being completed or plugged, which the definition ('after the drilling and completion of the initial test well') states slightly more narrowly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean residual definition keyed to whether Operating Rights have been earned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 2(D), 3(B)(1) and 5(B); the only friction is that acreage 'earned' is measured by circles, so unearned land is defined by subtraction from a plat.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Gross proceeds attributable to the sale or production from a well' set against 'the cost of drilling, completing and equipping' leaves open whose costs, whether operating costs count, and whether gross or net proceeds control.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Payout is the trigger for the royalty escalations in Section 4.A, so any looseness here propagates directly into the parties' principal money term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commence the actual drilling' by a date and completion within 45 days of total depth are definite, though no depth obligation is stated for the test well.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) lists 3(A)(2) as a provision under which the Agreement 'terminates' even though 3(A)(2) contains no termination language, and Section 16 conditions the ROFR on the test well being drilled and completed by August 31, 1996, which 3(A) does not require.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Farmee shall have the option ... and, at Farmee's further option, it shall continuously develop' mixes permissive and mandatory language in one sentence about the same obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) treats 3(B)(3) as a termination trigger for 'Farmee's failure to meet the drilling commitments', which presupposes a binding commitment the clause itself calls an option.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Lost for any reason' and a 'formation or condition which would render further drilling impractical or impossible' are judgment-laden standards a farmee could invoke broadly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties to Contract Depth in 2(F) and interacts with the time-of-the-essence default clause 3(F), giving a 30-day cure route that 3(F)'s automatic termination does not expressly acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within sixty (60) days after Farmor is satisfied' makes delivery turn on the Farmor's own subjective satisfaction, while (2) runs a different 60-day clock from completion, and forfeiture follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The forfeiture in (2) sits uneasily with 4.A's survival of royalties and with 3(F)'s preservation of 'Operating Rights Earned', and it incorporates Exhibit C's open-ended geologic requirements by reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise depth formula with a numeric cap; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D reserves everything below a blank-named formation, which may not correspond to the 4,000-foot/100-feet-below-TD line set here and in 2(F).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence terminates automatically for drilling failures while the second gives a 30-day notice and cure for defaults 'other than above', so which regime governs a mixed breach is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) cross-refers to 3(F), and the takeover right here is made 'subject to the terms of Section 6', but Section 6 by its terms addresses only takeovers elected 'under ... Section 5'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Gross proceeds ... without deductions of any kind', 'Farmor reserves the right to escalate', and the garbled 'less than one hundred percent (100%) or the working interest' are precisely the phrases parties fight over in royalty disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D's royalty paragraph repeats 'without deductions of any kind' but adds a severance-tax exception absent here, and the escalations depend on the loose 'Payout' definition in 2(K).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Ceases production' and the telephone/48-hour rig-on-location alternative are workable, though 'take over the well for the purpose of conducting additional operations as it desires' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5(A) makes silence a deemed election not to take over, i.e. requires only notice, while 5(B) penalises plugging without 'Farmor's approval' — the two set different conditions for the same act.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fails to give Farmor a reasonable opportunity to consider its options' is a vague standard bolted onto the specific notice mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It demands 'written notification and Farmor's approval', but 5(A) requires only notice and treats Farmor's silence as an election not to take over, so approval is never required there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any Operating Rights Earned by Farmor and earned by Farmee' is garbled, and 'estimated salvage value ... less estimated plugging costs' leaves the estimator unidentified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(F) allows Farmor to take over wells on default 'subject to the terms of Section 6', yet Section 6 opens by addressing only elections made 'under the terms and conditions of Section 5'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shut in for any reason', a $500 'per well per year, prorated on a monthly basis' rate, and payment 'by the last day of each month' pull against each other on how much is owed when.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2(H) defines a 'shut-in well' as one that 'has previously produced', while this clause expressly covers wells 'whether or not such well has already produced'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When possible' is an open-ended qualifier that all but dissolves the ten-day notice obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with 7(A)'s shut-in royalty and 5(A)'s notice regime without contradicting either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully enumerated indemnity; 'of any kind or character' follows a list, and there is no negligence carve-out, but the reach is broadly drawn rather than uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with 8(B), Section 9's no-warranty term and Exhibit D's indemnity in favour of Assignor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line absolute covenant to keep the lands free of 'all liens'; simple and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D gives the Assignor a lien on future production for unpaid royalties and 15(D) separately bars Farmee-created liens, so the absolute covenant needs harmonising with liens the Farmor itself takes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Does not warrant title, either express or implied' is grammatically off (warranties, not the verb, are express or implied), but the disclaimer's effect is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D repeats a fuller disclaimer, and nothing elsewhere promises title, so the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite one-year confidentiality period tied to well completion; 'unless otherwise agreed ... in writing' is a normal carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes well notices to Exhibit C, whose delivery address and attention party differ from the notice block in 10(B), a minor inconsistency in where information must go.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare address block with no stated method of delivery or deemed-receipt rule, which leaves 'shall be given as follows' doing more work than it can bear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C D.1 directs reports to a different street address and a different individual, and 5(A) permits telephone notice, so this is not the only notice channel.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insurance covenant names coverage types but no limits, amounts or terms, so 'acquire and/or maintain' has no measurable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the indemnity in 8(A) without contradicting it; nothing elsewhere sets limits either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading 'Modifications and Amendments' does not match the content, which is an after-acquired-interest clause reaching 'any subsequently acquired interest ... whether obtained directly or indirectly'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement contains no actual amendment or integration clause, so a reader relying on the heading finds none; the substance extends Section 4.A's reserved royalty into new interests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall be in effect until such time as' followed by two alternatives is workable, but the clause supplies no outside date and hinges on cross-references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 3(A)(2) and 3(B)(3) as provisions under which the Agreement 'terminates' although neither contains termination language, and 3(B)(3) frames continued drilling as an option, so the trigger for expiry is genuinely uncertain.
